trust_decision.summary: Runtime values are meant to reach SQL only through positional `?` placeholders rendered by escapeValue (single-quote wrapping plus quote doubling), while raw SQL fragments, identifiers and the `sql` tag are trusted developer input; the boundary fails because ClickHouse also honours backslash escapes, JSON payloads are pasted unescaped inside quotes, and nothing validates the raw/identifier routes.

landing_point.why: The advisory is titled 'SQL injection in parameter escaping'; a reader looks first at escapeValue's string branch, which only doubles single quotes and ignores backslashes.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared scanner used by where()/prewhere()/having()/withScalar() composition (new file utils/sql-parens.ts)
.having(condition[, parameters]) when several fragments are combined

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can dismiss the second implementation because measure-level filter values are developer-authored in the measure definition and the project spec calls custom SQL in field definitions trusted code, and because the `sql` tag / expr.raw() are documented escape hatches, so 'only escapeValue is user-data territory'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The `sql` tagged template and expr.raw()/having() strings are raw-SQL authoring routes that must keep inserting interpolated strings verbatim, and the existing where suite pins exact SQL for logical groups ('(hasAny(tags, [\'foo\'])) OR (status = \'active\')'); a fix that escapes raw strings or blanket-wraps every fragment breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: string with a trailing backslash (C-style escape swallowing the closing quote)
string containing both backslashes and single quotes
object/array values JSON-serialized inside a quoted literal (quotes in nested values)
null rendered as NULL and undefined rejected instead of stringified
non-finite numbers (NaN, +/-Infinity) and invalid Date instances rejected
`?` occurring inside string literals, quoted identifiers, $tag$ heredocs, or comments
AND/OR at paren depth 0 of a raw fragment, versus inside parens/brackets/literals/comments/heredocs/unicode quotes
trailing line comments (--, //, #, #!) at the end of a composed fragment
unsafe identifiers supplied as CTE alias or predicate function name

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate literal renderer in @hypequery/datasets: filtered-measure string values are interpolated with quote-doubling only, no backslash escaping
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: filter values come from developer-authored measure definitions (packages/datasets/src/measure.ts:11), not from request input
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one module in a separate package (packages/datasets); never passes through the clickhouse renderer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: formatDateTime() interpolates developer-supplied format and timezone strings into quoted literals with no escaping
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: format strings are code-level constants passed to a SELECT-expression helper, and ClickHouse requires the format as a string literal
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different module (utils/sql-expressions.ts vs core/utils.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Identifier protection added for CTE alias and fn() name is missing for aggregate aliases and columns
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: alias and column arguments are typed by schema-derived TypeScript template literals, so they are treated as compile-time-trusted identifiers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: rawAs()/selectExpr() append an unchecked alias to a raw expression
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: part of the documented select-expression escape hatch, the alias is a developer-chosen string
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same module as the formatDateTime route

O8_uncovered_routes.route: sql`` tagged template inserts interpolated strings as raw SQL text
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the published fix chose to re-document this as an intentional raw-SQL authoring API (fix.diff:948-951) instead of changing it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate dataset module in the same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an inline-literal IN/array renderer that concatenates escaped values instead of emitting a list of `?`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: IN-list inlining is a common ClickHouse perf tweak and the datasets/serve packages already render literal lists this way

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a countIf/sumIf helper that inlines a predicate string built from a filtered measure
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: filtered measures already exist in @hypequery/datasets and countIf is the natural ClickHouse idiom for them

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SETTINGS clause values concatenated as `${key}=${value}` from a config object
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: settings are already rendered straight from queryNode.settings with no validation or quoting

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new select-expression helper that inlines a label, timezone or interval option next to the field
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every date helper in this file follows the same rawAs(<interpolated string>, alias) template

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89): missing neutralisation of string literals, raw predicate fragments and identifiers in generated SQL

services: ClickHouse server for the integration suite only (packages/clickhouse/scripts/run-integration-tests.js; skipped when SKIP_INTEGRATION_TESTS=true)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Double backslashes in escapeValue and stop: keep `sql.split('?')`, leave the JSON-in-quotes branch, the flat AND/OR concatenation and the datasets/serve literal copies untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/cli/src/generators/clickhouse.ts:198 escapes quotes inside ClickHouse type strings for generated TypeScript; that is codegen hygiene, outside this advisory's protection, and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured without shell access, so O4.repo_mb is null and tiny_repo/giant_repo were not evaluated.

Fix-diff base mismatch: the query-builder.ts hunks import './insert-builder.js' and the predicate-builder.ts/query-builder.ts hunks import assertSafeIdentifier from './utils/insert-identifiers.js', and neither module exists at the pinned commit, so those hunks were written against a newer base; the utils.ts, predicate-builder.ts, sql-formatter.ts and analytics.ts hunks do match the pinned tree line for line.

O12 interpretation note: query-builder.where.test.ts:370, 414 and 449 already exist at the pinned commit and the fix changes their expected strings, but the fix's added #348 regression block and the new utils/sql-parens tests are absent, so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit was not raised; the detail is recorded in O5 instead.

Whether the datasets/serve literal copies should count as in-scope defects rests on the measure-filter values being developer-authored; that was established only by reading measure.ts, types.ts and query-planner.ts, not by tracing a request path.

ClickHouse's exact runtime acceptance of a trailing backslash inside a literal was not executed (no running of project code); the claim rests on the fix's changelog and the project's own regression tests in the diff.
